verdict.rationale: First-party docs show researchers can upload their own PDFs and other document formats as sources, with per-source limits of up to 500,000 words or 200MB. They can then chat with grounded, inline-cited answers, choose which sources the model uses, and generate briefings or reports. Community users call it genuinely useful for structured research and note it holds a lot of context. missing for 10: independent hands-on evidence of multi-step agentic research across a large corpus (support is shown as grounded Q&A and report generation), and smooth ingestion of non-file corpora such as email archives.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can upload my own PDFs or corpus and have the agent research over them

citations.quote: Easily upload PDFs, websites, YouTube videos, audio files, Google Docs, or Google Slides or discover new sources.
Each source can contain up to 500,000 words or up to 200MB for uploaded files.
Chat with your notebook to get grounded information based on your sources with clear in-line citations for accuracy, transparency, and trust.
Select which sources in your notebook the model should use to answer your questions.
NotebookLM is genuinely useful for structured research workflows.
